script:
Presenter: Mariam, I heard your class helped at the heritage guesthouse last week. How did that start?
Mariam: Our teacher asked us to learn what welcoming visitors is really like, so we arranged a visit and met the hotel supervisor.
Presenter: Was it just a tour, or did you get to try anything?
Mariam: We did a short training session on Thursday afternoon. We practised greeting guests and explaining local customs.
Presenter: That sounds useful. Did the staff give you anything to work from?
Mariam: Yes, we were given visitor information cards. The supervisor checked the details with us first.
Presenter: What sort of things did you have to explain?
Mariam: Simple things, like where to find places nearby and how to behave respectfully at local sites.
Presenter: Did everything go smoothly?
Mariam: Not quite. We noticed that one booking time on our information sheet was wrong.
Presenter: Oh, that could have caused a problem for a visitor.
Mariam: Exactly. We checked the confirmed reservation, corrected the notice and told the rest of the group.
Presenter: Was anyone annoyed that you had to change the sheet?
Mariam: A little, because we had already printed copies. But it was better to fix it than leave incorrect information.
Presenter: What did the supervisor say about dealing with visitors?
Mariam: He said people have different needs, so we should listen first instead of making assumptions.
Presenter: Did you have a chance to practise that?
Mariam: Yes. One visitor needed extra support, and we learned to ask politely what would help.
Presenter: How did you divide the work?
Mariam: Some students checked facts, some prepared the cards, and others practised conversations with guests.
Presenter: Did you get feedback at the end?
Mariam: We did. We wrote it down and changed a few explanations that were not clear enough.
Presenter: Are you going back?
Mariam: Next term, we hope to help with a guided visitor welcome programme.
Presenter: What will you take away from the experience?
Mariam: Accuracy and patience matter. A friendly welcome is important, but the information must be right too.
